topic: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange for delegation chains
title: Token Exchange — OAuth 2.0
snippet: RFC 8693 defines a protocol for exchanging one security token for another, including delegation semantics. The specification defines a protocol for an HTTP- and JSON-based Security Token Service (STS) by defining how to request and obtain security tokens from OAuth 2.0 authorization servers, including security tokens employing impersonation and delegation.
claim: RFC 8693 is the governing standard for OAuth 2.0 token exchange with support for delegation

topic: act claim for delegation chains in JWT
query: RFC 8693 act claim nested delegation token composition
title: RFC 8693 Deep Dive: Token Exchange - DEV Community
snippet: The act (actor) claim provides a means within a JWT to express that delegation has occurred and identify the acting party to whom authority has been delegated. A chain of delegation can be expressed by nesting one act claim within another. The outermost act claim represents the current actor while nested act claims represent prior actors.
claim: RFC 8693 supports nested act claims to express delegation chains with current actor in outermost position

query: SPIFFE SPIRE workload identity X.509 SVID 2026
title: An overview of the SPIFFE specification
snippet: SPIFFE (Secure Production Identity Framework for Everyone) is a set of open-source standards for securely identifying software systems in dynamic and heterogeneous environments. SPIRE is a production-ready implementation of the SPIFFE APIs that performs node and workload attestation in order to securely issue SVIDs to workloads.
claim: SPIFFE is a standard for workload identity with SPIRE as production implementation issuing X.509-SVIDs

query: agent identity delegation chain OpenID Connect
title: OpenID Connect for Agents (OIDC-A) 1.0: A Standard Extension for LLM-Based Agent Identity and Authorization
snippet: OpenID Connect for Agents (OIDC-A) 1.0 is an extension to OpenID Connect Core 1.0 that provides a comprehensive framework for representing, authenticating, and authorizing LLM-based agents within the OAuth 2.0 ecosystem. OIDC-A addresses the unique requirements of autonomous agents, including their varying degrees of autonomy, operation within complex delegation chains, and dynamic capabilities.
claim: OIDC-A 1.0 extends OpenID Connect to represent agent identity and delegation chains in OAuth 2.0 ecosystem

query: workload identity federation modern standards practices
title: What is Workload Identity Federation? A Complete Guide
snippet: Workload Identity Federation is an authentication mechanism that allows applications, services, containers, CI/CD pipelines, AI agents, and workloads to access cloud resources without storing long-term credentials. Standards like OpenID Connect (OIDC) and SPIFFE workload identity specification concepts standardise workload provenance.
claim: Workload Identity Federation uses OIDC and SPIFFE standards for ephemeral, attribute-scoped workload authentication

topic: X.509-SVID certificates for mTLS workload identity
query: SPIFFE SPIRE workload identity X.509 SVID 2026
title: X509-SVID | SPIFFE
snippet: X.509-SVID is an X.509 certificate in which the SPIFFE ID is embedded in the Subject Alternative Name (SAN) field as a URI. SVIDs are short-lived (1 hour by default), automatically renewed, and tied to the workload's identity. This integrates directly with mutual TLS (mTLS) — the standard mechanism for service-to-service authentication.
claim: X.509-SVID enables mTLS-based service identity with short-lived automatic renewal tied to workload attestation
